newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST- Portugal Sept inflation seen 0.0-0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Portugal Sept inflation seen 0.0-0.3 pct.

text.p: Portuguese consumer price inflation should be between 0.0 and 0.3 percent in September, compared with 0.3 percent in August, analysts said.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) is due to release September inflation figures at 1400 GMT today.
"The increase in tobacco prices felt in recent months will not be felt this month, and so the monthly change should be zero," said Isabel Cabral, economist with Lisbon broker Fincor.
But other analysts were watching changes in the food and drinks sector to determine what CPI would be in September.
Isabel Ramos de Almeida of Banco Totta e Acores said "The food and drinks heading should have stabilised in the month of September, and the monthly change should be 0.2 percent."
Nuno Botelho of Banco Mello de Investimentos said "The consumer price index should have grown by 0.1 percent in September, with a zero change in food and drinks."
Monthly inflation between 0.0 and 0.3 percent in September would bring Portugal's year-on-year inflation rate to between 3.5 and 3.8 percent and average annual inflation to 3.3 percent.

In August, year-on-year inflation was 3.6 percent and average inflation was 3.3 percent. In September, 1995 prices rose 0.2 percent, the year-on-year rate was 4.0 percent and average annual inflation was 4.2 percent.
